subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Holiness
overview: Holiness means being set apart for God and keeping away from sin. In this sub-strand you will read 1 Corinthians 6:19-20, learn that the body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, describe ways of glorifying God with the body, and practise staying away from situations that lead to sin.

lessons.title: The body is the temple of the Holy Spirit
objectives: Explain what the verse teaches about the body.
lessons.intro: A temple is a holy place set apart for God. In 1 Corinthians 6:19 Paul tells Christians that the body itself is the temple of the Holy Spirit. That teaching changes how a young person treats the body.
lessons.notes:
### The verses to read
Read 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 in pairs. In simple English the verses say:

"Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own? For you were bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body."

The learning outcome asks you to recite verse 19, the part about the body as the temple of the Holy Spirit. Learn it until you can say it without the book.

### What the words mean
- A temple is a holy place where God is worshipped. The verse says the Christian's body is that kind of place, because the Holy Spirit lives in the believer.
- The Holy Spirit is from God. He is not a feeling we invent.
- "You are not your own" means a Christian belongs to God. The body is not for any use a person feels like choosing.
- "Bought with a price" means a great price was paid so that we could belong to God. Christians understand this price as what Jesus Christ did when he died for us.
- "Glorify God in your body" means honour God by the way you use your body.

### Lessons from the reading
- The body is holy, not something to be misused.
- What we do with the body matters to God, because his Spirit lives in the believer.
- We honour God with the body. We do not live as if the body has no master.
- Holiness begins with knowing whose we are.

Take turns to read. Let each learner say the verse, then listen while a partner says it. Humility here means not rushing, not laughing at a classmate who is still learning the words, and waiting for your turn.

keyWords.meaning: a holy place set apart for God
the Spirit of God who lives in the believer

activity.title: Read and recite 1 Corinthians 6:19-20
steps: In pairs, read 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 aloud, taking turns.
Mention the lessons learnt from the two verses.
Write 1 Corinthians 6:19 on a flash card and recite it until you can say it from memory.
Tell your partner one way the verse teaches you to treat your body.

practice.question: Recite 1 Corinthians 6:19.
practice.answer: Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own?

practice.question: According to the verse, whose temple is the body?
practice.answer: The temple of the Holy Spirit.

practice.question: What does "you are not your own" mean for a Christian?
practice.answer: A Christian belongs to God. The body is not for any use the person feels like choosing.

practice.question: What does verse 20 tell Christians to do with the body?
practice.answer: Glorify God in the body, because they were bought with a price.

summary: 1 Corinthians 6:19 says the body is the temple of the Holy Spirit.
Christians belong to God; they were bought with a price.
Therefore they glorify God in the body.

lessons.title: Glorifying God with the body
objectives: Describe ways of glorifying God with the body.
Explain what it means to desire a life free from sin.
lessons.intro: If the body is God's temple, then hands, mouth, eyes, ears and feet can honour him. Glorifying God with the body means using each part for what is good and refusing what is sinful.
lessons.notes:
### Ways to glorify God with the body
1 Corinthians 6:20 says, "Therefore glorify God in your body." These are ways a Grade 4 learner can do that.

- Keep the body clean. Bathe, wear clean clothes, brush the teeth and cut the nails. A place set apart for God is not left dirty.
- Use the hands to help, to write and to work. Do not use them to steal, to hit or to damage property.
- Use the mouth to tell the truth, to pray, to sing and to speak kindly. Do not use it to insult, to lie or to speak dirty words.
- Use the eyes and ears for what is good. Turn away from pictures, films and talk that lead you into sin.
- Eat, rest and play in healthy ways. Do not put alcohol, cigarettes or other drugs into the body.
- Dress decently.
- Keep the body sexually pure. Do not take part in sexual acts. The body belongs to God.
- Use the feet to walk away from a place where you are being tempted.

### A life free from sin
Holiness is being set apart for God. A holy life is a life that is not held by sin. Young people can desire this. Desire means you want it and you choose it, even before anyone forces you.

Wanting a holy life shows in small choices: you wash, you tell the truth, you refuse a bad picture, you stop a fight, you pray. You will still make mistakes. When you do, you do not stay in the sin. You tell God you are sorry and you turn back. The desire is to be free from sin, not to pretend you have never failed.

Glorifying God is not a show for visitors. It is how you live on an ordinary school day because the Holy Spirit's temple should honour God.

keyWords.meaning: set apart for God and kept from sin
clean in God's sight; not used for sexual sin or other wrong
to want something and to choose it

activity.title: Ways of honouring God with the body
steps: In pairs, list ways of glorifying God with the body, using hands, mouth, eyes, ears and feet.
Put a star next to one way you will practise this week.
Sing a song on holiness that you know from church or Sunday school.
Say together: we desire to lead holy lives free from sin.

practice.question: Give three ways of glorifying God with the body.
practice.answer: Any three: keep the body clean, use the hands to help, speak kindly and truthfully, turn away from bad pictures, avoid drugs, dress decently, keep sexually pure, and walk away from temptation.

practice.question: How can the mouth glorify God?
practice.answer: By telling the truth, praying, singing and speaking kindly, and by refusing insults, lies and dirty talk.

practice.question: What does it mean to desire a holy life free from sin?
practice.answer: To want to be set apart for God and to turn away from sin, even when no one is forcing you.

summary: Hands, mouth, eyes, ears and feet can honour God.
Cleanliness, helpful work, pure speech and sexual purity glorify God.
A holy life is one that keeps turning away from sin.

lessons.title: Keeping away from situations that lead to sin
objectives: List sins that do not please God.
Describe how to keep away from situations that lead to sin.
lessons.intro: Sin does not usually begin with a big plan. It often begins in a situation: a dare from friends, a hidden place, a film, or a secret. Holiness grows when we keep away from those situations.
lessons.notes:
### Sins that do not please God
God is holy, so sin does not please him. In pairs, learners can list sins such as these:

- Lying and cheating
- Stealing
- Disobeying parents, guardians and teachers
- Hatred, fighting and bullying
- Insults and dirty talk
- Sexual sin
- Refusing to forgive
- Loving wrong things more than God

This list comes from what Christians know displeases God. It is not a verse number to memorise. The point of the list is to recognise sin early and refuse it.

### Situations that lead to sin
A situation is a moment or a place that makes sin easier.

- Friends who dare you, laugh at you for saying no, or plan a wrong act
- Lonely or hidden places where no trusted adult can see
- Films, pictures, songs and chats that show or encourage sin
- Long empty time with nothing good to do
- An older person who offers gifts and says, "Do not tell your parents"
- Anger that is left to grow until it becomes a fight

### How to keep away
- Choose friends who want to do right.
- Say no in a clear voice and leave the place.
- Do not go to a hidden place with someone who makes you uneasy.
- Switch off a bad film or walk out of the room.
- Keep busy with homework, chores, games and church.
- Pray and ask God to keep you.
- Tell a parent, guardian or teacher. A person who tells you to hide a wrong act from your parents is not keeping you holy.

Acquiring holiness means these steps become your habit. You do not wait beside the temptation and hope you will be strong. You keep away.

keyWords.meaning: thoughts, words or actions that displease God and break his teaching
a place, a group or a moment that can make sin easier
to stay out of a place or a plan that leads to sin

examples.problem: Friends say, "Come behind the classroom. We have pictures the teacher must not see." What should a learner who wants to be holy do?
steps: Hidden places and bad pictures are situations that lead to sin.
Holiness means keeping away, not going to look and then deciding.
The learner should refuse, leave, and tell a trusted adult if the pressure continues.
examples.answer: Say no, do not go behind the classroom, and tell a parent or teacher if they keep pushing.

activity.title: Sins to refuse and situations to avoid
steps: In pairs, list sins that do not please God.
In groups, discuss how to avoid situations that lead to sin.
Write three situations and, beside each one, the step you will take to keep away.

practice.question: Name four sins that do not please God.
practice.answer: Any four, for example lying, stealing, disobedience, fighting, dirty talk, sexual sin, and refusing to forgive.

practice.question: Give two situations that can lead a learner into sin.
practice.answer: Any two: bad company and dares, hidden places, bad films or pictures, idleness, or a secret that must be hidden from parents.

practice.question: What should you do when friends dare you to do wrong?
practice.answer: Say no, leave the place, choose better friends, and tell a trusted adult if they continue.

summary: Sins such as lying, stealing, disobedience, hatred and sexual sin do not please God.
Hidden places, bad pictures and pressure from friends lead towards sin.
Holiness means saying no, leaving, and telling a trusted adult.

lessons.title: Choosing a holy life
objectives: Explain how a young person can desire and live a holy life.
Plan daily habits that keep a person away from sin.
lessons.intro: Holiness is not only for adults in church. First Corinthians 6:19-20 speaks to believers about their own bodies. A Grade 4 learner can desire a holy life and practise it day by day.
lessons.notes:
### What a holy life is
A holy life is a life set apart for God and free from holding on to sin. "Free from sin" does not mean a learner has never done wrong. It means the learner does not want sin, does not stay in it, and keeps turning back to God.

The desire comes first. You decide that you want to please God. Then the habits follow. Without the desire, rules feel like a burden. With the desire, the same rules become a way of loving God.

### Daily habits
- In the morning, pray: "God, help me to glorify you with my body today."
- Recite 1 Corinthians 6:19 so that you remember whose temple the body is.
- Think before you join a group, open a video or answer a dare.
- Keep your body clean and your words clean.
- If you sin, admit it quickly, ask God to forgive you, and do the right thing instead. If you lied, tell the truth. If you took something, return it.
- Stay near people who help you do right: parents, teachers and friends who obey God.
- Sing about holiness. A song can remind you of the choice when the lesson is over.

### When the situation is already tempting
Do not argue for a long time. Leave. Joseph, in the story the class has read, ran from the room. You can do the same kind of thing: step away from the phone, the picture or the hidden place. Then tell someone you trust.

Leading a holy life as a young person protects you, honours God and helps your friends. One learner who says no can give another learner the courage to say no too. That is how holiness builds a peaceful class.

keyWords.meaning: something you do so often that it becomes your usual way
kept for God and not mixed with sin
God's pardon when a person turns away from sin

activity.title: A song and a promise of holiness
steps: In groups, discuss one habit that will help you avoid situations that lead to sin.
Each learner writes one sentence beginning, "I desire to lead a holy life by..."

practice.question: What is a holy life?
practice.answer: A life set apart for God and not held by sin.

practice.question: What should a learner do after falling into a sin?
practice.answer: Admit it, ask God for forgiveness, turn away from it, and do the right thing, such as telling the truth or returning what was taken.

practice.question: Name two daily habits that help a young person stay holy.
practice.answer: Any two: morning prayer, reciting 1 Corinthians 6:19, thinking before joining a dare, keeping body and words clean, staying near people who do right, and singing about holiness.

practice.question: Why should young people lead holy lives?
practice.answer: The body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, so they glorify God, keep away from sin, and help others to do right.

summary: A holy life is set apart for God and keeps turning away from sin.
Prayer, clean habits and quick repentance help a learner live that life.
When temptation is near, leave the situation and tell a trusted person.

quiz.question: Complete 1 Corinthians 6:19: "Your body is the temple of _____."
quiz.explanation: The verse says the body is the temple of the Holy Spirit.

quiz.question: Recite 1 Corinthians 6:19.
quiz.answer: Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own?
quiz.explanation: Learners are to recite this verse on the body as the temple of the Holy Spirit.

quiz.question: "You are not your own" means:
options: The school owns every learner's clothes
Parents may not guide their children
quiz.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:19 says the believer belongs to God.

quiz.question: Which action glorifies God with the body?
options: Telling the truth and keeping the body clean
Watching a bad film in secret
quiz.explanation: Cleanliness and truthful speech honour God with the body.

quiz.question: How can the hands glorify God?
quiz.answer: By helping, writing and working, and by refusing to steal, hit or damage property.
quiz.explanation: Glorifying God with the body includes using each part for good.

quiz.question: Which of these is a sin that does not please God?
quiz.explanation: Lying is a sin. The other actions are good.

quiz.question: Friends call you to a hidden place to look at bad pictures. What should you do?
options: Go, but only for a minute
Say no, leave, and tell a trusted adult if they insist
quiz.explanation: Holiness means keeping away from situations that lead to sin.

quiz.question: Why should you not keep a bad secret for someone who wants you to do wrong?
quiz.answer: That secret hides sin. A trusted parent, guardian or teacher should be told.
quiz.explanation: Keeping away from sin includes refusing secret plans.

quiz.question: What does it mean to desire a holy life free from sin?
options: To claim you have never done wrong
To want to be set apart for God and to turn away from sin
quiz.explanation: Desire means wanting and choosing a life set apart for God.

quiz.question: Give one habit that helps a learner lead a holy life.
quiz.answer: Any one: daily prayer, reciting 1 Corinthians 6:19, refusing dares, keeping the body and speech clean, or telling a trusted adult.
quiz.explanation: Habits turn the desire for holiness into daily life.
